name: Superscalp
tagline: A scalping-oriented trading tool for short-timeframe traders, sold as a paid product.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Anything in the fast-trading tooling category splits into two halves, and only one of them is buildable. The cockpit half, live order book, hotkey order entry, position sizing, a trade journal, risk limits, is a genuinely good weekend project against a crypto exchange API with a websocket feed. The signal half, whatever edge or indicator logic is being sold, is not something you clone by asking an agent nicely, and if it is a discretionary strategy wrapped in software then the software was never the point. Public detail here is thin, so treat the specifics as unverified and assume any latency, data feed, or broker connectivity claims are the part that costs money. Build the cockpit, keep your own strategy, and expect the connectivity to be where the weekend goes.
coreLoopDIY: A local trading cockpit that streams one venue's order book and trades, lets you fire preset-size orders with hotkeys, enforces hard risk limits, and logs every fill to a journal you can actually review.
requirements: An exchange or broker account with API access and, ideally, a testnet or paper environment
API key and secret in .env, permissions scoped to trading only, never withdrawals
A machine that stays awake and a connection you trust
Your own strategy: the build gives you execution and discipline, not an edge
whatYouLose: Whatever proprietary signal or indicator logic the paid product actually sells, which you cannot reverse engineer from a homepage
Colocation, low-latency routing, and any infrastructure that makes fills better than your laptop's fills
Broker and venue coverage beyond the one API you wire up, plus the maintenance when that API changes
Mobile access and alerts while you are away from the desk
Someone else on the hook when the order router misbehaves during a fast move
moatNotes: Execution tooling lives or dies on connectivity and behavior under stress, which is exactly what a one-shot build does not get tested for.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a trader losing money does not want to also be debugging their own websocket reconnect logic at 2am, and because most of these products are really selling a method with a UI attached. The tooling is the delivery mechanism for the claim that someone has figured out short-timeframe trading. You can rebuild the delivery mechanism in a weekend. You cannot rebuild the claim, and you should probably be suspicious of it either way.
notes: The cockpit is a weekend, the edge is not for sale in a repo, and any product promising both deserves a slow read of its disclaimers.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user scalping cockpit for one crypto exchange. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Node 22 + TypeScript, one repo, one process for the backend (Fastify) and Vite + React + Tailwind for the UI.
- ccxt for REST order placement, native ws client for the exchange websocket feed.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for the trade journal. No ORM.
- Config and secrets in .env only: EXCHANGE_ID, API_KEY, API_SECRET, USE_TESTNET, SYMBOL.

Default to the exchange testnet and refuse to start against live keys unless LIVE_CONFIRM=yes-i-mean-it is set.

In scope:
- Websocket order book (top 20 levels) and trade tape for one symbol, rendered at 10fps max, no layout jank.
- Position and balance panel polled every 2s, plus unrealized PnL.
- Hotkey order entry: keys for buy market, sell market, join bid, join ask, flatten, cancel all. Sizes come from three preset risk tiers defined in a config file as percent of equity.
- Hard risk guards enforced server side, not in the UI: max position size, max open orders, max daily realized loss, and a kill switch that cancels everything and blocks new orders for the rest of the session.
- Trade journal: every submitted order, fill, and cancel written to SQLite with timestamp, symbol, side, size, price, and a free-text note field. A journal page with per-day realized PnL and a simple win-rate table.
- Reconnect logic with exponential backoff and a visible, unmissable STALE banner when the feed is older than 2s.

Out of scope, do not build: any signal generation, indicator, or auto-trading loop; multiple exchanges; backtesting; mobile; auth; charts beyond a sparkline.

Deliver: README with setup, .env.example, npm run dev, and a DANGER section stating plainly that this places real orders when configured to and that the risk guards are best effort, not guarantees.
